subject: Trying to understand a renderUI and conditionalPanel combo

messages.author: d0fbfb6af4d40394
messages.subject: Trying to understand a renderUI and conditionalPanel combo
parts:
Hey Y'all,

I just posted a question on stackoverflow, but I figure that I should try my luck here as well. I'm trying to make a shiny app that utilizes both renderUI and conditionalPanel at the same time.

Here is the link to my stackoverflow post: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/38409404/shiny-if-statement-with-input-variable-in-server-r-might-be-null?noredirect=1#comment64228048_38409404

below is my isolation of the problem:

ui.R contains the following three relevant chunks of code:


      radioButtons('view', 'View U.S.A data according to state or region:', c('states', 'regions'), 'regions'),

      conditionalPanel(
        "input.view == 'states'",
        uiOutput('state')
      ),

      conditionalPanel(
        "input.view == 'regions'",
        uiOutput('region')
      ),
and server.R contains the following two if-statements and two renderUI statements:

  output$state <- renderUI({
    selectInput(inputId = 'location',label = 'Choose a state:', choices = location, selected = location[1])
  })


  output$region <- renderUI({
    selectInput(inputId = "area", label =  "Choose a region:", choices =         c("Midwest", "Northeast",
                 "South Central", "South Atlantic", "West"), selected =  "Northeast")
  })


    if(input$view == 'regions'){

      bar_mcgun <- bar_mcgun %>% filter(region == input$area)

    }

    if(input$view == 'states'){ 

      bar_mcgun <- bar_mcgun %>% filter(state == input$location)


    }


      ggplot(bar_mcgun, aes(state, value, fill = as.factor(variable))) +
        geom_bar(stat = 'identity', position = 'dodge')


I think that putting the uiOutput in the conditionalPanel may be hiding the inputid's and preventing me from accessing them. When I try to call input$area or input$location I get NULL


Any advice would be awesome.

messages.author: d0fbfb6af4d40394
messages.subject: Re: Trying to understand a renderUI and conditionalPanel combo
parts: I figured it out. It was a mixture of me not really understanding reactive statements. Once I figured out reactivity I ran into another one regarding dplyr: it's really hard to use dplyr in a shiny reactive statement so I just replaced filter() with the base filtering method.

messages.subject: Re: Trying to understand a renderUI and conditionalPanel combo
parts:
Glad you were able to figure out the problem regarding reactives. Hopefully you are using reactive() and not observe().

What do you mean about dplyr? Is it because you can't hardcode the column names you're filtering? Sometimes it helps to use the dplyr verbs with a trailing underscore, e.g. filter_.
